key_insight: PRISM uses a transformer to decode erasure-dominated quantum errors, matching integer-programming decoders’ logical error rates while running significantly faster.
engineering_relevance: An optimized AMD VP1902 FPGA implementation demonstrates 6.59 µs latency and 1.56 µs amortized decoding time per logical block at distance 8 in space and time.
method: Exploit known erasure locations to decode combined Pauli and erasure errors.
Benchmark across surface codes, color codes, and quantum low-density parity-check codes.
Optimize the decoder and FPGA implementation for low-latency inference.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks cover code distances up to 24 and error rates up to 50% of threshold, with logical error rates matching integer-programming-based decoders.
watch_item: The reported FPGA timing is for distance-8 blocks; comparable real-time performance at larger code distances remains to be demonstrated.
paper_title: Machine-learning decoders for fusion-based quantum computing in real time
